items: Review no longer merges two different facts: "reads news every morning" and "reads papers every morning" both stay. Lines 0.4.0 merged by mistake are put back by themselves.
Cortex's own tidying shows in your sessions as "Cortex tidied lines about you", not as an AI chat, and each Review answer is one Undo.
Status tells you when Claude Code runs an older Cortex than the app; its Fix puts the app's copy first.
Review's More fold no longer repeats Today's cards, and its buttons say Keep first and Keep second.
Lines that try to steer an AI are also refused when they say "act as DAN" or start with a chat label such as "assistant:".
do: If Status shows a Claude Code row, press Fix, then quit Claude completely and open it again.

items: Review finishes: Cortex keeps one of lines that say nearly the same and settles replaced lines itself. It asks only when two of your own lines clash, one answer covers every rewording, and after Today's 5 it says Done for today.
What chats learn about you is saved at once as a guess; your own words always win over it. Teaching rules, your core and your setup still wait for your click.
Every AI app knows how you work: Claude, Cursor, Codex and VS Code get your profile, preferences, setup and playbooks (a note tagged playbook: how you want a kind of task done).
The local Chat knows who is asking and answers counts and timelines from your notes. The new Tonight tab shows your day, Today's 5 and what AI apps learned about you today, with Undo.
Agent X-ray shows what each AI app was given (pin, mute, scope, dry run), and lines that try to steer an AI ("ignore previous instructions") are refused and never reach another app.
The Cortex capture browser extension is gone. Your history still comes in by itself from your browsers: every 10 minutes while the app runs, and from the receiver when it starts at login.
do: On Status, press Fix on the Claude Desktop row if it shows, then restart Claude once.
If you had "Cortex capture", remove it from your browser's extensions page.

items: Cortex shows as Cortex: its own Cortex.exe and logo in the title bar, taskbar, Start menu and Task Manager, and pinning it pins Cortex.
Import my past history goes on from where you paused it, and never shrinks or redoes days an earlier import already wrote.
Settings opens at once: Setup, Local model and Browsing no longer wait about 3 seconds on each visit.
A Claude Chat-tab chat and its claude.ai export are one chat page, not two.
Next up lines wrap instead of cutting off, and the brain's legend starts folded on smaller screens.
do: If you pinned Cortex to the taskbar before, unpin it and pin it again, so the pin shows the new logo.

items: Cortex is its own app: a window and a tray icon, it starts with Windows, and closing the window keeps it running.
The first page is your live brain: what you did today and this week, Next up, exams and deadlines. New pages pop in by themselves.
Your browsing is the brain stem: one dot per site, sized by visits and glowing by how recently you went there. Click one to see its days and searches.
A Private switch behind Windows Hello shows private notes and sites; it locks again when you minimise or after 10 minutes.
Every chat is logged: past and new Claude Code, Desktop and Cowork chats import themselves every 5 minutes, and the Chat tab logs itself.
Plans have no dates: each subject is an ordered list, the one you studied last comes first, and nothing is ever behind.
do: Restart Claude once after this update, so its Cortex tools use the new version.
Reload the browser extension (Extensions page, Reload) if you use it.

items: The dashboard feels like the app: buttons react, keyboard focus is easy to see, and copy buttons confirm with a check.
Status warns when your browsing history has not been imported for a while, with Import new history now.
Chat lists the sites you visited and sums up a day or week in about a second, even on a big history.
Browser profiles you untick in the history list stay unticked in every automatic import.
Chat understands more dates ("on Monday", "last night", "the last 3 days", "what's due on Friday?") and a day starts at 04:00, as in Today.
Sites filed under a category you set to Don't save never show in Chat's site lists or summaries.
do: Your first browsing import after this update rebuilds every day your browsers still hold, once, so it takes longer than usual.

items: Chat shows what it is doing while an answer is on its way, and how long the answer took.
Esc stops an answer, every answer has Copy, and scrolling up no longer drags you back down.
"Which sites did I visit?" lists every site once, most visited first; name a browser to see only its visits.
New browser history comes in by itself every 6 hours while the app or the receiver runs (Browsing, Past history).
Chat answers "What should I study today?", "what's due?" and "summarize my week" from your own plan and records.
The browser extension only sends its key to your own Cortex receiver, never to another program on that port.
do: Reload the Cortex browser extension: open your browser's Extensions page and click the reload arrow on Cortex.
To keep history coming in without the app open, turn on Start at login under Browsing.
